summary: Candidate sources for New Brunswick, Middlesex County hospital resource simulation. The sources located do not provide local inventory, lot-level expiry, replenishment events, or maintenance windows for RWJUH or Saint Peter’s. FDA device recalls can support external device risk/recall scenarios; AHRQ MEPS supplies a national household benchmark for medical equipment and supply spending; the 2023 National Blood Collection and Utilization Survey offers national blood collection and transfusion context. These are discovery leads, not acquired datasets or local calibration values.

sources.title: Medical Device Recalls API
sources.geography: United States; no hospital inventory or Middlesex County stock data
sources.period: 2002 onward; API updated weekly. Page inspection reported coverage through 2026, with end date rendered as null.
sources.grain: Device recall record; not local item, location, lot-on-hand, maintenance, or replenishment event
useful_fields: manufacturer and FDA-harmonized identifiers where present
observed_facts: FDA describes the API as converted JSON with added openFDA fields and weekly updates.
FDA warns against using this data to issue public alerts or track recall lifecycle; recall status is not subsequently updated in the Enforcement Reports.
The API query pattern is verified as https://api.fda.gov/device/recall.json with search and limit parameters; no API key is required to try the API.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Bound a public query to device product codes relevant to the two selected simulated procedures, retrieve a small capped set of recall records, retain query URL and retrieval date, and use only as an external recall-risk scenario. Independently verify product-code relevance before mapping to simulated equipment.
limitations: National regulatory recall records do not establish whether either named hospital owns or uses a device, its lot, or operational status.
Recall records are not a maintenance schedule, inventory feed, or real-time alert source.
Device compatibility rules require a clinical source and domain-owner review; recall product-code mapping alone is not a compatibility rule.

sources.title: MEPS HC 254C: 2024 Other Medical Expenses — documentation and public-use file
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
sources.geography: United States, civilian noninstitutionalized population; no hospital or Middlesex County estimates
sources.grain: Person-reported other-medical event record; not hospital procurement, per-unit consumption, or item-location inventory
observed_facts: The public-use documentation describes purchases or obtaining of glasses/contact lenses, ambulance services, disposable supplies, and long-term medical equipment.

The data are event-level and include weighted expenditure and source-of-payment variables; the documentation says the actual number of purchases is not collected, so per-unit prices cannot be estimated from these records.
The documentation distinguishes payments from charges and cautions that charges do not generally represent actual dollars exchanged or resource costs.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Download the 2024 Other Medical Expenses public-use file and codebook from the AHRQ file-detail page; restrict analysis to disposable supplies or long-term medical equipment, apply survey weights for national context, and keep spending separate from hospital supply costs or quantities.
limitations: Household survey data do not represent hospital supply use, procedure-specific consumption, lot expiry, procurement lead times, or equipment uptime.
The data do not support a New Brunswick or facility-level estimate.
Do not infer unit counts or unit prices from expenditures.

sources.title: 2023 NBCUS findings on blood collection and utilization
sources.publisher: America’s Blood Centers, summarizing the 2023 National Blood Collection and Utilization Survey paper in Transfusion
sources.geography: United States aggregate; no New Jersey, Middlesex County, or hospital-specific values established from the inspected source
sources.grain: National annual aggregate counts and proportions of blood components collected, distributed, transfused, or outdated; not item × location × lot × event
useful_fields: whole-blood and apheresis red blood cell collection and transfusion totals
platelet unit distribution and transfusion totals
observed_facts: The inspected summary reports participation representing 96% of community-based blood centers and 85.7% of transfusing hospitals.
It reports 11.586 million whole-blood and apheresis RBC units collected in 2023, and 10.328 million transfused, with RBC transfusions down 4.1% from 2021.
It reports 2.618 million platelet units distributed and 2.220 million platelet units transfused in 2023; these are national aggregates.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use the cited Transfusion paper link on the inspected summary to determine whether its tables or supplemental materials are openly downloadable; if publicly accessible, collect only the national annual aggregate fields needed for a clearly labeled external benchmark. Do not extrapolate those totals to either hospital.
limitations: The inspected source is a secondary summary of a national survey; the underlying paper or supplement was not independently opened or verified here.
No local hospital or county blood inventory, component compatibility, expiration distribution, or replenishment data are supplied.
Not directly comparable to a facility stock fixture without local item-level calibration.

missing_inputs: Facility-specific blood-component inventory by component, ABO/Rh, location, lot, quantity, and expiry for RWJUH and Saint Peter’s.
Local issue, transfusion, wastage/outdating, transfer, and replenishment events with timestamps and units.
Procedure-to-item and equipment compatibility rules reviewed by qualified clinical or biomedical engineering owners.
Equipment asset inventory by location, availability state, uptime, planned maintenance windows, failures, and repair duration.
Local supplier and blood-provider lead times, order quantities, substitutions, and shortage episodes.
Publicly downloadable New Jersey or Middlesex County facility-level blood collection and utilization data were not established in the bounded search.
simulation_use: Treat the public sources as context only. For the requested synthetic fixture, label all stock quantities, lots, expiry dates, replenishment timing, equipment states, uptime, and maintenance windows as synthetic. Keep item taxonomy separate from clinical compatibility; require an authoritative clinical source and domain-owner review before enforcing any procedure-resource rule. Inventory the listed local inputs needed for calibration, without implying that such values are publicly available or observed at either facility.
limitations: No source inspected provides the required local grain of item/equipment type × location × lot/state × replenishment event.
FDA recalls, MEPS expenditure events, and national NBCUS aggregates cannot calibrate local stock quantities, expiry, maintenance windows, uptime, or supplier lead times.
All source candidates require independent verification for current availability, field definitions, and redistribution terms before acquisition.
